stories.headline: Taiwan indicts ex-TSMC manager in first China trade-secret theft case under security law

key_facts.fact: Taiwanese prosecutors on Monday (July 20) indicted a former TSMC deputy manager, surnamed Chen, for allegedly attempting to leak TSMC's core chip technologies to China
key_facts.excerpt: A former executive at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has been indicted for allegedly attempting to leak TSMC's core technologies to China, prosecutors said Monday.

key_facts.fact: Chen was charged under the National Security Act and the Trade Secrets Act, with prosecutors requesting a seven-year prison sentence
key_facts.excerpt: the former deputy manager, surnamed Chen, has been charged with violating the National Security Act and the Trade Secrets Act and that prosecutors have requested a seven-year prison sentence.

key_facts.fact: Prosecutors call it Taiwan's first prosecution involving an alleged attempt to transfer national core critical technology trade secrets to China
key_facts.excerpt: It is Taiwan's first prosecution involving an alleged attempt to transfer national core critical technology trade secrets to China, the indictment said.

key_facts.fact: Between May 2023 and February 2024 Chen allegedly copied 21 confidential TSMC documents to help establish a semiconductor materials analysis company in China; TSMC detected the breach and recovered all documents before any transfer
key_facts.excerpt: Chen allegedly made unauthorized copies of 21 classified and general trade-secret documents belonging to TSMC... TSMC detected the irregularities through an internal investigation and recovered all of the copied documents before any technology was transferred.

key_facts.fact: The case emerged from a separate probe into an alleged Chinese espionage network in Taiwan run by Hong Kong national Ding Xiaohu
key_facts.excerpt: The case emerged from a separate investigation into an alleged Chinese espionage network in Taiwan developed by Hong Kong national Ding Xiaohu.

stories.headline: China's Z.ai completes 1GW data center built entirely on domestic chips to train GLM models

key_facts.fact: Z.ai (formerly Zhipu) has completed a 1-gigawatt data center that houses only Chinese-made chips and has begun partially operating it, a step in Beijing's push to replace restricted Nvidia silicon
key_facts.excerpt: Z.AI has completed construction of a giant data center that houses only Chinese-made chips... The company formerly known as Zhipu has begun partially operating the 1-gigawatt hub designed to help the Chinese company develop its cutting-edge GLM platforms.

key_facts.fact: The site runs several computing clusters, each holding more than 10,000 chips, none of them Nvidia's; 1GW is roughly the power draw of 750,000 homes
key_facts.excerpt: Z.AI now runs several computing clusters, each holding more than 10,000 chips... Crucially, none of them are Nvidia's. A gigawatt is roughly the power draw of 750,000 homes at any one moment.

key_facts.fact: Z.ai shares surged 37% in Hong Kong on Tuesday to close at HK$1,219 (US$155) after reports of the data-center completion, rebounding from a week-long drop of more than 40%
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Chinese AI giant Z.ai soared 37 per cent in Hong Kong on Tuesday to close at HK$1,219 (US$155), after the company recently completed a giant data centre powered entirely by Chinese chips.

key_facts.fact: Z.ai also completed the acquisition of XCore Sigma, a heterogeneous-computing software developer spun off from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, to improve utilization of mixed domestic chip clusters
key_facts.excerpt: the Beijing-based company had also completed the acquisition of Chinese infrastructure software developer XCore Sigma... XCore Sigma focuses on heterogeneous computing software, including compilers, runtime systems and inference engines that help improve the utilisation of AI chips from different vendors.

key_facts.fact: Details rest on a single anonymous source; no independent party has verified the chip count, named the accelerators, or shown the power source, and Z.ai has not confirmed them
key_facts.excerpt: the load-bearing details are unconfirmed. No independent party has verified the chip count, named the accelerators, or shown where a gigawatt of power is coming from.

stories.headline: China weighs export controls on chip designs and AI models, consulting Alibaba, ByteDance, Zhipu

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce has been consulting leading domestic AI and chipmaking firms on tightening export controls to keep advanced Chinese technologies and startups from being acquired by the West, the FT reported
key_facts.excerpt: Regulators led by China's Ministry of Commerce have been consulting top homegrown AI and chipmaking companies on how to stop China's advanced technologies and leading start-ups from being acquired by the west.

key_facts.fact: Officials sought views on restrictions that would prevent overseas chipmakers including TSMC and Qualcomm from producing advanced semiconductors based on designs developed by Chinese firms such as Huawei, Alibaba and ByteDance
key_facts.excerpt: It has also sought views on possible restrictions that would prevent overseas chipmakers including Qualcomm and TSMC from producing advanced semiconductors based on designs developed by Chinese companies such as Huawei, Alibaba and ByteDance.

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Ministry also discussed limiting overseas transfer of key model-training data and restricting foreign users from downloading Chinese firms' model weights
key_facts.excerpt: MofCom has reportedly spoken with the likes of Alibaba and ByteDance on limiting the transfer of key data for the training of their models overseas and allowing their model weights to be downloaded by foreign users.

key_facts.fact: The measures could be added to the next revision of China's catalogue of technologies prohibited or restricted from export, with regulators still weighing industry feedback
key_facts.excerpt: The new measures could be included into the next revision of China's catalogue of technologies prohibited or restricted from export, the report said, adding that these proposals are under consideration.

stories.headline: TSMC to raise chipmaking prices by up to 10% from 2027 across advanced and mature nodes

key_facts.fact: TSMC plans to raise prices for both advanced and mature chip production by up to 10% in 2027 to reflect rising costs for materials, equipment and overseas plant construction, Nikkei Asia reported July 21
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is set to raise prices for both advanced and mature chip production services by up to 10% in 2027 to reflect rising costs for materials, manufacturing equipment and construction of new overseas chip plants.

key_facts.fact: Base price increases range from 5% to 10% depending on customer and product; mature-node production (12nm, 16nm, 28nm) faces increases of up to 10%, with new pricing taking effect at the start of 2027 after negotiations that began in June and concluded in July
key_facts.excerpt: The base price increases range from 5% to 10%, depending on the customer and product... Mature-node production, covering 12-nm, 16-nm and 28-nm technologies, faces increases of up to 10%... Negotiations began in June and concluded in July, with new pricing set to take effect at the start of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Customers including Apple, Nvidia and AMD have been informed of the planned increases; orders for high-performance computing chips above original forecasts could carry an additional 10% to 15% premium
key_facts.excerpt: customers including Apple, Nvidia and AMD have been informed of the planned increases. Orders for high-performance computing chips above original forecasts could carry an additional 10% to 15% premium.

key_facts.fact: The hikes follow TSMC's record second quarter, when profit jumped 77% to T$706.6 billion (about $22 billion)
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, TSMC... surpassed market expectations to post a 77% jump in second-quarter profit touching a record high of T$706.6 billion ($22 billion).

stories.headline: South Korea chip exports jump 180% to record $22.1B in first 20 days of July on AI demand

key_facts.fact: South Korea's semiconductor exports totaled $22.1 billion in July 1-20, up 180.6% year-on-year, a record for the period, per Korea Customs Service preliminary data released July 21
key_facts.excerpt: Chip exports totaled $22.1 billion, up 180.6% from a year ago, setting a new record for the July 1-20 period.

key_facts.fact: The chip surge was driven by rising fixed prices for memory chips and growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI servers and solid-state drives
key_facts.excerpt: Rising fixed prices for memory chips, along with growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI servers and solid-state drives, drove the increase.

key_facts.fact: Semiconductors made up 40.3% of total exports; overall exports hit an all-time high of $54.9 billion for the period, up 52.3% year-on-year
key_facts.excerpt: Semiconductor exports jumped 180% to 22.1 billion dollars... Semiconductors accounted for 40.3% of total exports... exports during this period increased by 52.3% year-on-year to 54.9 billion dollars.

key_facts.fact: Computer peripheral exports more than tripled (+231.9%) to $2.04 billion, and semiconductor-equipment imports rose 56.9% to $2.15 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Computer peripheral exports more than tripled to $2.04 billion... imports of chipmaking equipment increased 56.9 percent to $2.15 billion.

stories.headline: BlackRock leads $12B+ bond sale to finance Meta's El Paso AI data center

key_facts.fact: BlackRock is seeking to sell more than $12 billion of bonds to help finance a Meta data center campus in El Paso, Texas, with total financing that could approach $13 billion
key_facts.excerpt: BlackRock Inc. plans to sell more than $12 billion in bonds to finance a data center campus in El Paso, Texas... the financing could reach approximately $13 billion.

key_facts.fact: The bonds are issued via a holding company for BlackRock's 80% stake in Project Sopaipilla Holdings; Meta owns 20% and will lease the roughly 1-gigawatt campus back
key_facts.excerpt: BlackRock and its infrastructure and private-credit arms own 80% of the roughly 1-gigawatt project, while Meta, the company that will actually run AI workloads inside it, owns just 20% and will lease the campus back.

key_facts.fact: BlackRock's 80% is held by funds run by Global Infrastructure Partners and HPS Investment Partners, both now units of BlackRock; JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are arranging the sale, with pricing expected early next week
key_facts.excerpt: Funds managed by Global Infrastructure Management, known as GIP, and HPS Investment Partners hold the 80% stake... The bonds are scheduled to be priced early next week.

key_facts.fact: The structure keeps most construction debt off Meta's balance sheet, recorded as rent rather than capital spending, echoing a nearly $30 billion Meta-Blue Owl deal last year for a Louisiana site
key_facts.excerpt: It follows a nearly $30 billion debt package completed by Meta and Blue Owl Capital last year to finance another large-scale data center project in Louisiana.

stories.headline: Gritt exits stealth with $34M for AI robots that build solar plants

key_facts.fact: Gritt exited stealth Tuesday (July 21) with a $26 million Series A led by Obvious Ventures, with Union Square Ventures and Active Impact Investment participating, bringing total funding to $34 million
key_facts.excerpt: The company exited stealth Tuesday morning with a $26 million Series A round of funding led by Obvious Ventures with participation from Union Square Ventures and Active Impact Investment. That brings its total funding to $34 million.

key_facts.fact: The startup was founded by Carnegie Mellon-trained roboticists Puneet Puri (CEO) and Vishal Dugar (CTO) and builds AI-controlled systems using off-the-shelf hardware such as robotic arms from Kawasaki
key_facts.excerpt: Founded by Carnegie Mellon-trained roboticists Puneet Puri, chief executive, and Vishal Dugar, chief technology officer, Gritt is building AI-controlled systems for construction sites using off-the-shelf hardware such as rented skidders and robotic arms from companies including Kawasaki.

key_facts.fact: Gritt's deployed systems let an eight-person crew install 3,000-4,000 solar panels a day, versus roughly 800 with traditional methods
key_facts.excerpt: Gritt's deployed systems enable an eight-person crew to install 3,000-4,000 solar panels daily, compared to the traditional 800 panels, significantly increasing installation productivity.

key_facts.fact: The company is contracted for 2.8 GW of solar installations over 18 months and plans to operate 48 systems within six months
key_facts.excerpt: Gritt is contracted for 2.8 GW of solar installations over 18 months, plans to operate 48 systems in six months, and targets expanding into additional construction automation tasks.
